entries.english:
(Co-)plaintiffs / petitioners / interveners: Abbot Hieronymus II and the convent of the Cistercian monastery of Ebrach (Abbot Wilhelm I of Ebrach, defendant and counter-plaintiff at first instance)
(Co-)defendants / interveners: Provost Johann Gottfried Ignaz Wolfskeel von Reichenberg, the dean and chapter of the collegiate foundation of St. Johann im Haug in Würzburg (Provost Christoph Franz von Hutten, plaintiff and counter-defendant at first instance)
Plaintiff's procurators: Lic. Ferdinand Wilhelm Brandt and (substitute) Lic. (Johann Paul) Besserer (1755); Lic. Johann Adolph Georg Brandt (1786); Lic. Johann Adolph Georg Brandt and (substitute) Lic. P(hilipp) J(akob) Emerich (1791); Lic. Franz Carl Brandt and (substitute) Dr. Johann Wilhelm Mainone (1798)
Defendant's procurators: Dr. Johann Jakob von Zwierlein and (substitute) Dr. Georg Melchior Hofmann (1760); Lic. Henrich Joseph Brack and (substitute) Lic. Johann Conrad Jakob Adami (1788)
Contemporary subject of dispute: appeal
Modern subject of dispute: hunting and boundary dispute.
Subject at first instance: In a dispute between the plaintiff monastery and the community of Fahr over the right to impose fines at Elgersheim, the Haug provost's office ruled against Ebrach in 1697, whereupon Ebrach appealed to the prince-bishop's government in Würzburg. After a commission of seven had acted in 1703, in 1718 the government awarded the monastery the disputed woodland district “Urlaß” and “Bandwehr(d)” and the lower hunting rights at Elgersheim. The defendant foundation then obtained a decree of review, under which that judgment concerned only the Haug community of Fahr and left the foundation's own rights unaffected. Later in 1718, the defendant foundation petitioned the government concerning a driven hunt held by the plaintiff monastery from the Elgersheim monastery farm, while the plaintiff monastery counter-sued over the impounding of fifteen hunting nets. After delays in the proceedings, Ebrach brought an action for declaratory judgment in 1733. The government ordered the defendant foundation to prove its claimed exclusive hunting right at Elgersheim, ultimately found the submitted evidence insufficient, required the defendant foundation to return the hunting nets seized in 1718, required the plaintiff monastery to return a gun impounded in 1750, and directed it to pursue its claims concerning the boundary district.
The abbot and convent consider themselves aggrieved by the grant of a shared hunting right to the defendant foundation and the reopening of the boundary dispute. The defendant foundation also appealed to the Imperial Chamber Court but did not pursue its appeal further.
Instances: 1. Prince-Bishop's Government of Würzburg, 1718 (according to the Rationes decidendi of 1733)
2. Imperial Chamber Court, 1760–1802 (1760–1798)
Enclosures to the plaintiff's petition (Q 10): undated charter of Abbot Konrad I of Ebrach concerning the transfer of Elgersheim by Arnold von Rothenburg; correspondence between Provost Franz Christoph von Rosenberg and Edmund Stepper, Ebrach official at Sulzheim, concerning a hunting incident in 1676; witness statements before a notary and the Vizedomamt in Würzburg, 1787 (Q 41).
Enclosures to the supplement to the reply (Q 43): charter of Bishop Hermann I of Würzburg concerning Count Rupert zu Castell's recognition of the immunity from bailiff jurisdiction of Ebrach's properties at Kaltenhausen (in the file: Husen), Untereisenheim, Fahr, and Elgersheim, 1225 (no. 8); purchase contract between Abbot Hermann II of Ebrach and Count Friedrich zu Castell for the “Urlaß” woodland near Fahr, 1301 (no. 9); correspondence between Stepper and Johann Philipp Gampert, the comital Castell chancellery director at Rüdenhausen, 1675–1688 (nos. 10–12); correspondence between Provost Otto Philipp Freiherr von Guttenberg and Abbot Paul II of Ebrach, 1713 (nos. 15–17).
The earlier file (Q 47) also contains: witness statements before the Haug official at Fahr and before a notary, 1746 (enclosure to no. 15), and before the government, 1750 (no. 23); ruling by an arbitration court under Jakob Honnaf, Schultheiß of Astheim (in the file: Ostheim), in the dispute between the parties over grazing, cutting reeds, and pasturing on “Bandwehr(d),” 1467 (enclosure no. 2 to no. 33); letters of command from Bishops Konrad Wilhelm and Johann Gottfried II of Würzburg to the officials at Volkach, Prosselsheim, and Schwanfeld to protect Haug hunting rights against encroachments by the Counts of Castell, 1690 (enclosures nos. 8 and 9 to no. 33; also Q 27).
Rationes decidendi, 1792 (Q 48).
